newsitem.title: CANADA: Bid target Merfin up on Q1 earnings rise.
newsitem.headline: Bid target Merfin up on Q1 earnings rise.

text.p: Shares of takeover target Merfin International Inc were slightly firmer in heavy trading on Tuesday after the specialty fabrics maker announced record first-quarter earnings.
Merfin was up 0.05 at 6.45 in Toronto and was among actives. The company announced earlier its first-quarter profits rose 68 percent to C$1.5 million.

Global Securities analyst Marcel Brichon said the stock action likely reflected the strong earnings rather than any developments related to Buckeye Cellulose Corp's C$6 a share takeover bid for Merfin.
Merfin has urged shareholders to reject the offer, which values it at about C$150 million. Memphis-based Buckeye said earlier today that its offer, which expires April 15, was "fair and full."
"I think the stock (activity) has more to do with the strong earnings," Brichon said. "The takeover has made people realize this is a good stock to hold."
In addition, the strong earnings could prompt a higher offer, either from Buckeye or another bidder, he said.
He said Buckeye's offer was widely viewed as insufficient. "Six dollars isn't enough. They could raise it or Merfin is looking for other possible suitors."

Merfin claims to be North America's biggest producer of air-laid specialty fabrics. The materials are used as absorbent cores for personal hygiene products and in premoistened towlettes and specialty wiping products.
The company plans to open a new plant in Ireland with production starting in the third quarter. This will make give it the second-biggest production capacity of air-laid materials in the world.
Merfin officials were not immediately available for comment.
